question: Can a response-conditioned acquisition scorer learned across training worlds choose 16 response locations that transfer to a reserved callable distribution better than equal-count random, a learned state-only design, and the frozen disagreement heuristic?

policy.model: ridge-linear with fixed lambda 1e-3 and training-only standardization

accessible_state: candidate x, x^2, norm, distance to initial support, and leave-one-selected-system-out RBF predictive mean/variance derived from initial observed responses
offline_reward: log reduction in aggregate selected-system error on a disjoint acquisition-validation bank after adding exactly one candidate state; all candidate responses are training-world-only
supplied_assumptions: exactly eight of sixteen systems retained
Legendre P3/P5 training and P7 reserved distribution
qualification: Tests learned acquisition within an engineered Legendre hierarchy and controlled resets. It does not establish calibrated uncertainty, passive inference, or arbitrary function discovery.
